title: V-type Atomic Variance Squeezing
authors: Chenrui Bi, Hong-Mei Zou, Zhao-Yang Tong, Zijin Liang
abstract: Variance squeezing of a V-type atom interacting with a dissipative cavity is investigated. First, the influence of atomic initial state parameters on the variance squeezing is explored. The results show that the atomic variance squeezing switches alternately between Sx and Sy as the initial state parameter alpha sweeps from -pi to pi. The two squeezing intervals are symmetric about alpha = pi/4, each with a width of pi/2. For alpha = pi/14, only the Sx component can generate variance squeezing and will eventually disappear with time evolution due to unavoidable environmental noise. Then, the influence of system parameters on the variance squeezing is also studied. It is found that, the optical variance squeezing depth of Sx is determined solely by the atomic initial parameters and is independent of the system parameters. Both weak cavity-environment coupling and atom-cavity detuning can significantly enhance the robustness of the Sx variance squeezing. The SGI parameter has an extremely weak influence on variance squeezing. These results are beneficial for high-precision quantum communication applications.
summary: This theoretical study analyzes variance squeezing in a V-type atom coupled to a dissipative cavity. It finds that while squeezing alternates between $S_x$ and $S_y$ based on initial conditions, the $S_x$ squeezing depth is robustly determined by initial states. Furthermore, the research demonstrates that weak cavity coupling and appropriate detuning can significantly enhance the longevity of this quantum resource.
main_problem: The paper investigates the variance squeezing of a V-type atom when it interacts with a dissipative cavity environment.
main_result: The $S_x$ variance squeezing depth is shown to be determined solely by the initial atomic parameters, independent of system parameters, while weak coupling and detuning enhance its robustness.
method: The analysis involves deriving the reduced density matrix and calculating variance squeezing factors using the Heisenberg uncertainty relation for spin components.
model_or_system: The system is a V-type three-level atom coupled to a single-mode dissipative cavity. The dynamics are governed by the system Hamiltonian and analyzed by tracing out the environment degrees of freedom.
key_observables: Variance squeezing factors ($V(S_x)$ and $V(S_y)$), standard deviations ($\Delta S_x, \Delta S_y$), and the expectation value $\langle S_z angle$.
important_parameters: Initial state parameter $\alpha$, cavity-environment coupling coefficient ($\kappa$), decay rate ($\gamma_0$), and detunings ($\Delta_1, \Delta_2$).
main_assumptions: The study addresses the open system nature due to dissipation, moving beyond previous closed-system assumptions.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the alternating nature of squeezing between $S_x$ and $S_y$ based on initial state parameters ($\alpha$), and show that $V(S_x)$ persistence is enhanced by weaker coupling ($\gamma_0/\kappa$) and increased detuning ($\Delta$).
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the theoretical framework for variance squeezing in the open system. It then analyzes the dependence on initial state parameters ($\alpha$), followed by a detailed study of system parameters, including coupling strength ($\gamma_0/\kappa$), the SGI parameter ($	heta$), and detuning ($\Delta$).
why_interesting: This work provides detailed insights into how dissipation and external control parameters (like detuning) can be leveraged to protect and enhance quantum correlations, which is crucial for quantum communication protocols.
